newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil barges fall on low demand, swaps.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil barges fall on low demand, swaps.

text.p: Euro high sulphur fuel oil barges slipped some $2 on Friday following falling swaps and with very low bunker demand as many players were absent due to the Assumption Day holiday.
High sulphur barges were offered higher early in the day at $97 and $97.50, or some 50 cents over Thursday's highest trade, but soon slipped to trade once at $95 and then $94.50 a tonne.
"The sellers began at $97 and $97.50 but after the deal at $95 by a major every one went lower. There are very few bunker enquiries," one trader said.
"Swaps came off and there's hardly any bunker demand and maybe some people are trying to push prices down. There's hardly any calls," a second trader said, explaining the move lower.
He put mid-day talk at $94/$95 for RMG material and $95/$96 for refinery material.
Most traders have said that the recent strength in the high sulphur barge market -- levels unseen since the start of spring -- had come from low prompt supply coupled with rising demand.
Traders said low sulphur barges were notionally unchanged in the absence of a real market, adding some sellers were still around $98 fob a tonne.

High sulphur fuel cargoes were also quiet with many traders absent due to the holiday. Levels were notionally unchanged for high sulphur cracked at about $92/$95 cif and for Russian material levels were put at about two means $2.50.

Russian high sulphur straight-run was unchanged but pressure loomed from thin buying interest, in particular from refiners who prefer to run crude, and several cargoes were still unsold, traders said.
